overall: The AG found the Ashland Select Board violated the OML by omitting a list of documents used from its January 17, 2024 executive session minutes, found the violation intentional, and recommended no civil penalty.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board's January 17, 2024 executive session minutes omitted a list of documents used at that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to list the document in the minutes of the meeting, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the list omission be found intentional; AG agreed, based on the Board's prior violation of the same provision within three years.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board was found in violation of the same provision of the Open Meeting Law less than three years ago, we find this violation intentional.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board waited over a year to create executive session minutes; AG did not reach it here, citing a separate determination.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent that the complaint alleges that the Board should not have waited over a year to create minutes of the January 17, 2024, executive session, that allegation was addressed in a determination issued by our office on May 30, 2025.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Amend the January 17, 2024 executive session minutes to include a list of all documents used at the meeting, and certify to the AG within 60 days.
remedy_passage: We further order the Board to amend the minutes of its January 17, 2024, executive session to include a list of all documents used at the meeting, and to certify to this office within sixty (60) days of the date of this letter that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
